hints: Notice the question asks for increasing wavelength, so start from the shortest wavelength end with gamma-rays and X-rays.
Recall that for all EM waves $c = f\lambda$, so shortest wavelength means highest frequency, with gamma-rays above X-rays in frequency.
Compare the remaining two: visible light has wavelength around $10^{-7} \text{ m}$ while microwaves are around $10^{-2} \text{ m}$, so visible light comes before microwaves.
walkthrough: List the four named regions: gamma-rays, X-rays, visible light and microwaves, and recall they all travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with $c = f\lambda$.
Increasing wavelength is the same as decreasing frequency and photon energy, so the highest frequency region comes first.
Gamma-rays have frequencies above X-rays, with wavelengths down to about $10^{-12} \text{ m}$ or less, so gamma-rays are the shortest wavelength of the four.
X-rays come next with wavelengths roughly $10^{-11} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, still much shorter than visible light at about $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Microwaves have wavelengths from about $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-1} \text{ m}$, much longer than visible light, so they are last in increasing wavelength order.
The order gamma-rays $\rightarrow$ X-rays $\rightarrow$ visible light $\rightarrow$ microwaves matches the list. This is option B.

options.A: This reverses the true order, placing longest wavelength microwaves first when increasing wavelength requires shortest first.
options.B: Gamma-rays have the shortest wavelength, then X-rays, then visible light, then microwaves with the longest wavelength of the four.
options.C: X-rays have longer wavelength than gamma-rays, and visible light has shorter wavelength than microwaves, so both pairs are swapped.
options.D: Microwaves and visible light are in decreasing wavelength order here, and gamma-rays have shorter wavelength than X-rays, not longer.
